title: Demystifying Artificial Intelligence
audience: Basic science learners building foundational AI literacy
objectives: Understand AI as a human-built tool for solving specific problems.
Recognize major milestones in AI history and how they shaped modern AI.
Practice evaluating AI claims as fact, fiction, misleading, or context-dependent.

sections.name: Interactive AI Timeline
sections.purpose: Give learners historical context for how AI capabilities developed over time.
sections.how_to_use: Scroll through the timeline milestones. Compare early symbolic systems, machine learning, deep learning, and generative AI.

sections.name: AI: Fact or Fiction?
sections.purpose: Help learners test assumptions about AI using structured feedback.
sections.how_to_use: Enter a statement about AI, then review the verdict, explanation, real-world examples, limitations, datasets, AI concepts, and research directions.

chatbot_guidance: When asked how to use the notebook, guide the learner through the timeline first, then the Fact or Fiction activity.
For basic science users, connect examples back to research design, data quality, model limits, reproducibility, and scientific discovery.
Keep answers short and practical. Ask one clarifying question only when the learner's goal is unclear.
Do not claim the Fact or Fiction verdict is definitive; remind learners it is AI-generated feedback that should be critically reviewed.

common_questions.question: How do I start?
common_questions.answer: Start with the timeline, then enter one AI claim in Fact or Fiction and review the feedback tabs.

common_questions.question: What should I type into Fact or Fiction?
common_questions.answer: Type a clear claim such as 'AI can discover new drugs by itself' or 'AI models always need labeled data.'

common_questions.question: What should I pay attention to?
common_questions.answer: Look for the verdict, the limitations, and whether the examples actually support the claim.
